name: Data center
summary: Colocation/hyperscale data centers are priced per kW of critical IT load; 70–85% of construction cost is electrical (switchgear, UPS, generators, distribution) and mechanical (cooling) infrastructure, so cost tracks IT capacity rather than floor area. Evidence is good: Turner & Townsend (US$13.28/W Chicago, 2026), JLL ($11.3M/MW shell-and-core, 2026) and Cushman & Wakefield ($17.6M/MW all-in, 2026) agree once scope differences (land, sitework, soft costs, contingency) are reconciled. Liquid-cooled AI halls carry a 7–10% premium; IT equipment is excluded.

typicalSize.method: Turner & Townsend benchmarks a typical 60 MW IT hyperscale facility (e7) = mid 60,000 kW; colocation buildings 10–40 MW, campus phases up to 200+ MW.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross building SF per kW of IT load. C&W ~$1,000/SF (e12) against $17,600/kW all-in (e1) implies ≈ 17.6 SF/kW; air-cooled hyperscale at ~150–250 W/SF of white space with white space ≈ 50% of gross ≈ 8–13 SF/kW; dense AI halls 5–7 SF/kW; older enterprise 20+. Mid 12 (judgment).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: kW of IT per site acre: single-story campuses with substations, generator yards and setbacks ≈ 0.5–2 MW/acre; multi-story urban 3–5 MW/acre (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Three reconciled anchors (all 2026 $/kW): (1) T&T US$13.28/W Chicago (e6; Silicon Valley $13.3 in 2025, e8) — includes GC contingency but excludes site works and fees (e7); (2) JLL shell-and-core $11.3M/MW global (e4) and US markets $10–$14M (e9); (3) C&W all-in $17.6M/MW (e1) less site acquisition 7% and ≈ 15–20% soft costs/owner contingency (e3 lists contingencies at 16%) ≈ $12.2k–$13.1k/kW. Mid $12,000 = between JLL US markets (~$11.5k NoVA) and T&T Chicago, plus ~3% typical sitework that T&T excludes. Low $9,000 = C&W all-in market floor $8.9M/MW (e2) for low-cost markets/simpler tiers. High $17,000 = high-cost market ($13.3k) + liquid cooling (+$1–2k/kW, e10; T&T 7–10%) + multi-story/sitework.

perSF.method: perPrimaryUnit ÷ sfPerPrimaryUnit at matched densities (12,000/12 = $1,000; 9,000/15 = $600; 17,000/9.5 ≈ $1,800). Consistent with the ~$1,000/SF attributed to C&W (e12); RSMeans 2019 small enterprise model ($307–$342/SF, e11) is a low-density outlier.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC preliminaries/OH&P: powered shell, white-space fit-out, electrical (MV switchgear, transformers, UPS, generators, PDUs/busway), mechanical cooling plant and distribution, fire protection/suppression, security, BMS/EPMS, and typical on-site work. Excludes land, IT/tech fit-out (servers, network, GPUs — up to $25M/MW for AI, e5), utility substation/transmission work, soft costs and owner contingency.

qualityTiers.method: economy = low/mid (Tier II/edge or low-cost market); premium 1.2 ≈ Tier IV / 2N redundancy or liquid-cooled AI (T&T 7–10% + $1–2k/kW, e7/e10); luxury = high/mid (multi-story, high-cost market, full liquid cooling).

systemSplit.method: ConstructConnect shares (specialty-mep block e10): electrical 48–54%, mechanical 22–33%, core & shell 9–14%. Mapped: electrical 26 (36%) + generators/power generation 48 (8%) + 27/28 (4%) = 48%; mechanical 23 (25%) + 21/22 (3%) = 28%; shell 03/05/07/08/09 = 13%; sitework 5%; GC 6%. C&W's "power infrastructure 21% of all-in" (e3) is consistent once land/soft/contingency are removed.

lineItems.name: Data-center MEP (electrical + mechanical infrastructure)

cost.method: From _blocks/specialty-mep.json data-center-mep ($5,000/$8,000/$11,500 per kW): mechanical $2–4M/MW + electrical $3–5M/MW; T&T $/W × 70–87% MEP share.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; includes the UPS and generator lines below.

lineItems.name: Standby diesel generators (N+1 ≈ 1.25 kW per kW IT incl. mechanical load share)

cost.method: From _blocks/specialty-mep.json emergency-generator ($350/$550/$750 per kW, 2014 $; escalated by the build). Recent switchgear/generator price inflation (+33% generators since 2021 per C&W/CRE Daily) suggests the escalated figure may still be low. Quantity 1.25 kW gen per kW IT (cooling load + N+1).

lineItems.name: UPS modules, batteries and bypass (per kW IT)

cost.method: From _blocks/specialty-mep.json ups-system ($600/$1,000/$1,500 per kW, derived as 20–30% of electrical). 2N designs roughly double this.

lineItems.name: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling premium (AI halls)

cost.method: Liquid cooling adds $1–2M per MW (e10) = $1,000–$2,000/kW; cross-check T&T 7–10% premium on ~$13.3k/kW (e7/e8) ≈ $930–$1,330/kW.

lineItems.notes: Optional; turn on for AI/high-density product.

lineItems.name: On-site HV substation / utility interconnection (optional)

cost.method: From _blocks/energy.json utility-interconnection ($30k/$100k/$250k per MW, 2022). Quantity ≈ 1.3 MW of utility capacity per MW IT (PUE ~1.3) = 0.0013 MW per kW. Often utility- or owner-funded and site-specific.

lineItems.notes: Off by default: substations/transmission are off-site-type costs excluded from the baseline.

pctOfHard.method: C&W all-in shares (e3) leave ≈ 10–15% of all-in for design, permits, commissioning and owner costs after construction, contingency and land; as a fraction of hard cost ≈ 8–18%. A/E for MEP-heavy design ~4–6%; integrated commissioning (Level 1–5) 1–2%; utility/power studies, permits and owner's rep the rest (judgment).

softCosts.notes: Type-specific soft items: utility power studies and interconnection deposits, Level 1–5 commissioning, ASHRAE/Uptime certification. Excludes IT equipment, land and financing.

hard.method: C&W reports contingencies at 16% of all-in cost (e3), which covers design, construction and owner contingency together; split as ~8% hard + 5% design + soft (judgment). Long-lead switchgear/generator risk.

perPrimaryUnit.method: C&W all-in market range $8.9M–$23.3M/MW (e2) incl. land; excluding land (~7%) and IT, hard+soft should fall ≈ $9.5k–$24k per kW.

evidence.quote: Developers can expect average greenfield costs of $17.6 million per MW for the most modern facilities.
evidence.scopeNotes: Cushman & Wakefield 2026 Data Center Development Cost Guide; all-in greenfield (incl. land/site acquisition, soft costs and contingency; excludes IT/GPUs). $17.6M/MW = $17,600/kW.

evidence.scopeNotes: Secondary report of the C&W 2026 guide market range; all-in incl. land and soft costs.

source.title: Data Center Construction Costs Jump 21% Since 2024

evidence.scopeNotes: C&W 2026 component shares of all-in cost (as reported by CRE Daily); MEP/soft-cost shares not given.
